location_note: Har Hozevim, north of Jerusalem on the road to Ramot; map ref. 1703/1347 (Old Israel Grid, 4-digit).
notes: First season at a Frankish (12th c.) farmhouse: vaulted main building, anterooms, courtyards; plaster platform with tabun; shallow rock-cut depression L117b (possible agricultural installation). Survey of the surroundings: quarries (some modern), large single cupmarks, quarry-debris heaps, two caves with rectangular openings and a fenced courtyard, field walls. A hole reported as a possible cistern was bulldozed before inspection; not coded.

features.subtype: quarries and quarry debris north-west of the site, large single cupmarks, shallow rock-cut depression L117b in the eastern courtyard
features.period: undated (quarries south of the site modern; L117b with the Frankish farmhouse?)
features.quote: The finds include quarries and their debris, cupmarks, caves and field walls.

features.subtype: two rock caves with large rectangular openings and a small fenced courtyard; recent use for prayer and seclusion
features.period: undated (no pottery); possibly connected with the farmhouse
features.quote: Two caves were found in the rock about 42 m northwest
